Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions are to register any questions via the telephone keypad at the appropriate time. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management Inc.'s Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Laura Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mark Thompson, Chief Investment Officer; Jane Doe, Head of Distribution; Tom Harris, Head of Operations; Emily Wong, Head of Risk Management; and David Patel, Head of Technology.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by a combination of favorable market conditions and our ability to attract meaningful organic net inflows. Our AUM grew to $1.2 trillion.

To give you a sense of our forward outlook, we're focused on delivering consistent AUM expansion through organic net inflows, market appreciation, and selective inorganic opportunities. As of quarter-end, total AUM reached a record $1.2 trillion, up 14% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. This blend includes about 9% from equity and fixed income gains, supported by the S&P 500's strength, and 5% from $42 billion in net client inflows, with $38 billion organic. Institutional AUM grew 11% to $780 billion, while retail and wealth management expanded 22% to $420 billion.

For FY24 and into early FY25, we see 11-13% AUM growth, targeting $1.4 trillion by year-end '25, assuming S&P up 7-9% and $55-70 billion annual net flows, with $45-60 billion organic—better than peers like BlackRock's recent figures. Inorganic adds could be $10-15 billion from our $2.5 billion dry powder.

Key levers include product momentum in passive and smart-beta ETFs at 28% of AUM or $336 billion, with $18 billion YTD inflows. Standouts like our Apex ESG Core Equity ETF have $12 billion AUM. Active alternatives surged 25% to $264 billion, with wins like $5 billion from pensions and $3 billion from SWFs. Our ApexOne platform has cut costs 22% and boosted retention to 97%. Robo-hybrid manages $65 billion.

Regionally, U.S. at 62% expects 10-12% growth from ETFs and DC plans. Europe 22% sees 8-10% via UCITS SFDR products. APAC 12% targets 15-18%. Distribution via RIA network generated $15 billion flows. Recent M&A like FinTech Alternatives added $20 billion. Risks include inflation and geopolitics, but our mix buffers us. We're guiding $55-65 billion organic FY24 flows.

Laura Chen: Thank you, Alex. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management Inc. delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $4.1 billion, representing an 11% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by AUM expansion and a slight mix shift to higher-fee products. Our expenses were $2.6 billion, resulting in net income of $1.5 billion. Our expense ratio improved due to scale and tech efficiencies.

Let me dive deeper into our efficiency ratios, focusing on the expense ratio as a key metric for investors in our industry, where fee pressures and operational leverage are critical amid the rise of passives and ETFs. Our weighted average expense ratio across $1.2 trillion AUM was 28 basis points for the quarter ended September 30, 2024, down 12% from 32 bps in Q3 2023. This is our 17th straight quarter of compression, beating Morningstar's industry average of 35 bps—tighter than Vanguard's 30 bps blended and competitive with BlackRock's iShares core at 15-25 bps, despite our 60% passive, 30% active, 10% alternatives mix.

By product, core ETF suite at 45% of AUM had 12 bps average, flat QoQ but down from 14 bps, with flagships like AAPX U.S. Equity ETF and EUGB Eurozone Bond ETF over $150 billion combined, spreading custody from State Street and licensing costs. Active equity and fixed income mutual funds at 25% of AUM were 58 bps, down 15 bps YoY via incentives and load waivers on $50 billion RIA flows. Alternatives at 1.25% or 125 bps matched peers like Blackstone, with 20 bps savings from co-investments.

Regionally, U.S. (65% AUM) at 22 bps from $200 billion inflows into target-date funds post-SECURE 2.0. Europe (20%) at 35 bps offset MiFID II and PRIIPs via UCITS ETFs undercutting competitors by 5-10 bps. Asia-Pacific (12%, 25% YoY inflows) at 45 bps, targeting sub-40 by FYE25 with Hong Kong hub.

Drivers include scale: 18% AUM growth diluted fixed costs 22%, expense-to-AUM at 24 bps vs. Lipper median 32 bps. Technicals: $250 million in digital transformation with Aladdin-like systems and AI optimizer shaved 4 bps; RPA for 70% middle-office cut headcount 15%; blockchain pilots cut T+1 costs 30%. Strategic waivers on $300 billion passives captured 12% U.S. large-cap share; active-to-passive conversions moved $40 billion to 18 bps smart-beta ESG.

Ahead, guide to 26 bps YE24, sub-25 bps YE25 with 10-12% AUM growth. Risks: inflation on comp (8% expenses), EU SFDR costs. Leverage: $100 billion AUM drops 2-3 bps. Primed for 45% adjusted operating margin FY25 vs. State Street 28 bps, Invesco 34 bps. This drives net returns, growth, value.

Turning to operating margin trends, we hit 36.2%, up 210 bps YoY from 34.1%, TTM 35.8% above 34-37% target and industry 32%. Average AUM $1.2 trillion up 14% levered fixed costs. Fee revenues $4.1 billion up 11% at 135 bps blended. Expenses up 7% to $2.6 billion: comp up 8% at 42% revenues, G&A up 5%. Active margins 38.5% up from 35.2%; passive 28%. Americas 39%, Europe 32% up 150 bps, APAC 34%. Digital Aligned platform cut costs 15%, 20 bps fee uplift; Horizon synergies $80 million added 100 bps. Alternatives 22% AUM at 42% margins. Q4 37-38%, FY25 36-38%.

On capital allocation, with $1.2 billion net cash from $2.8 billion FCF TTM, we prioritize shareholder returns (55%), organic growth (25%), M&A (15%), tech (5%) for >15% ROIC. Returned $1.1 billion YTD: dividend $0.42/share up 8% yielding 2.3%; $650 million buybacks retiring 2.1% float, ROE 18.2%. Organic to ETFs/alts with $120 billion inflows. M&A: $2.4 billion Pinnacle RIA added $65 billion, 7% EPS accretive. Tech $250 million GAP Horizon cut costs 18% to 22 bps. Flex for opportunities, 22% TSR past five years.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Laura. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by emphasizing disciplined alpha generation amid inflation, rate expectations, and geopolitics. We launched the Apex Sustainable Alpha Equity ETF this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $1.8 billion inflows.

Today, I'd like to highlight our new product launches and fund performance rankings driving organic growth and leadership in active/smart-beta. YTD, five strategies attracted $4.2 billion in first 90 days, 25% better than Q1. Flagship Apex Sustainable Alpha Equity ETF (GHSA equivalent, ticker APEXSA) launched March, blends active selection with AI ESG scoring for mid-cap clean energy, 0.28% expense, $1.8 billion inflows from RIAs/Europe SFDR compliant. Up 12.4% vs. MSCI ESG 8.2% on Enphase, batteries.

Apex Private Credit Opportunities Fund (May), semi-liquid interval, 9.2% yield, $1.1 billion from HNWIs/family offices, partnering Ares-like for $1.5T private credit. APAC: Apex Asia Ex-Japan Tech Innovators UCITS ETF $650 million on Nikkei surge. US retail via app up 35% fixed-income flows. Hybrids minimize tracking error <1.5%, 120-150% upside.

Performance: 78% equity strategies 4/5-star Morningstar 3-year, top quintile. Apex Global Equity Partners Fund (GHEP) Gold Medalist, Sharpe 1.12 vs. 0.89, 2.4% 5-year alpha on NVIDIA, TSM. Fixed income 85% top-quartile Lipper: Core Plus Bond 6.8% 1-year +180 bps Bloomberg, duration 5.2. Balanced Growth 5-stars 9.2% 10-year. Alternatives real estate 11.5% IRR +250 bps. Europe 65% top-quartile, APAC #1 ex-Japan. US retail $2.8 billion flows.

Pillars: personalization direct indexing $10B 2025; thematic AI/decarb 25% allocs NLP analysis; hedging cut vol 15%. $12.5 billion YTD flows strongest half, setting standard vs. T. Rowe, PIMCO.

Jane Doe: Thank you, Mark. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in Asia-Pacific are paying off, as evidenced by robust regional flows and client wins.

Our net flows were a highlight, $18.2 billion quarter, YTD $52.4 billion up 25%, 11th straight positive, 78% organic AUM growth. Ex-markets $32.7 billion add. Performance drove 45%: equities +320 bps, Pinnacle Global Equity 12.8% +4.2% MSCI on NVIDIA/ASML; Large Cap Growth Sharpe 1.85. Fixed: Core Bond 3.2% +110 bps.

Market trends: ETFs $7.2 billion up 40%, Pinnacle 500 $3.5 billion; ESG $2.1 billion SFDR; alts $2.9 billion private credit/infra. US 62% $11.3 billion wirehouses/RIAs; Europe $4.2 billion UCITS; APAC $2.5 billion 18% YoY.

Tech: PinnacleFlow AI 28% conversion lift $1.8 billion; ETF conversions $900 million; model marketplace $10 billion target. Institutional $1B+ mandates secondaries 15.2% IRR. Guide $20-25 billion/quarter FY25.

On client dynamics, retention 95.2% up 40 bps vs. 94.8% average, outperforming peers. Alpha 72% beat 3-year; cross-sell 2.8 products. Americas 96.1%, EMEA 94.3% UCITS, APAC 93.7%. AI retention 87% accuracy cut churn 22%; Next Best Action 35% engagement.

Acquisition $22.4 billion gross, net $18.2 billion: alts $9.8 billion evergreen oversubscribed; ESG $4.1 billion Climate Bond $1.8 billion; FI $3.9 billion; equities $2.5 billion. Institutional $3.5 billion Canadian; retail $2.8 billion Schwab/Fidelity. Americas 65%, APAC 40% QoQ $3.1 billion HNW transfer; EMEA $3.3 billion.

Levers: interval funds $2T market; RIA headcount double 28% conversion; Client360 CRM 12-18%. Guide $65-75 billion FY24 inflows, retention 95.5-96%. NPS 72 top decile, Q4 pipeline $35 billion.

Tom Harris: Thank you, Jane. Operationally, we've made significant progress in streamlining our middle and back office functions. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on enhancing scalability through tech integrations post-acquisitions.

Emily Wong: Thank you, Tom. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes dynamic hedging and stress testing.

David Patel: Thank you, Emily. On the technology front, we are investing in advanced analytics and AI to enhance our investment decision-making process and improve client service. We are also focused on strengthening our cybersecurity posture. Specifically, our Aladdin-like platforms, RPA, blockchain pilots, and AI optimizers have driven cost savings and alpha.

Alex Rivera: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes pursuing mergers and acquisitions for inorganic growth.

On M&A, key to scale/diversify high-fee AUM amid lumpy flows, 15% equity drawdown. Two Q3 closes added $62 billion, 8% pro forma. Horizon Alternatives Partners $1.2 billion, $28 billion AUM 85 bps fees, cross-sell to $450 billion alts, 98% retention, Aladdin migration 5-7% efficiencies. EMEA beachhead €2T illiquids L+450bps.

Pacific ETF Innovators merger $850 million shares, $34 billion AUM 28 bps, 15% EPS accretive $40 million saves. Thematic AI/clean energy $1.5T inflows. Co-branded UCITS/130-30. Industry M&A +25% YTD, alts mix to 22% 65 bps fees. Pipeline $15 billion APAC, $20-30 billion YE funded $2.5 billion powder. 95% retention track record.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Sarah Thompson with Morningstar.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on management's outlook for AUM growth?

Alex Rivera: Great question, Sarah. As I touched on earlier, our outlook is grounded in execution across products, tech, and distribution. Base case 11-13% to $1.7 trillion by '25 end, but detailed: organic $45-60 billion 3-4% rate top peers. Inorganic $10-15 billion. ETFs $20-25 billion new launches AI/Transition/Buffered. Alts private credit 32% growth. ApexOne OMS/PMS AI alpha, SMA scale 15,000 RIAs. Blockchain NAV tokenized $16T opp. U.S. 10-12% DC $25 billion; Europe 8-10% €8 billion; APAC 15-18% $2.5 billion China. RIA network $15 billion, M&A tuck-ins $50-100 billion. Q4 flows $14-16 billion, every 1% AUM +$120 million fees. Balance sheet $4.2 billion liquidity. Resilient to risks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. And a follow-up on your capital allocation strategy?

Laura Chen: Happy to, Sarah. As outlined, prioritize returns 55%—$1.1 billion YTD dividends up 8%, buybacks $650 million ROE 18.2%. Organic 25% ETFs/alts $120 billion inflows APAC $48 billion. M&A 15% Pinnacle-like 7% accretive, pipeline Europe quant/LatAm PE >20% ROIC. Tech 5% $250 million Horizon AI/ESG/blockchain cut 18% costs $1.2B/advisor density. Stress-tested 2.5x coverage, 22% TSR.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Bloomberg.

Mike Lee: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of Apex Global Equity Partners Fund?

Mark Thompson: Sure, Mike. GHEP earned Gold Medalist Morningstar, Sharpe 1.12 vs. 0.89 category, 2.4% 5-year alpha MSCI ACWI, overweight NVIDIA 150% YTD, TSM EM. Part of 78% 4/5-star equities, top quintile Barometer. Resilient Q1 vol max drawdown low.

Mike Lee: And how is the new product Apex Sustainable Alpha Equity ETF performing relative to expectations?

Jane Doe: Exceeding, Mike. $1.8 billion inflows 90 days, 12.4% inception vs. 8.2% MSCI ESG, institutional RIAs Europe SFDR. Complements pipeline, strong retail app adoption.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays.

Lisa Chen: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Tom Harris: Absolutely, Lisa. Streamlining middle/back office via RPA 70% functions, UiPath partnership 15% headcount save no service impact. Digital $250 million Aladdin/custom AI forecast automate expenses 4 bps save. Custody blockchain DTCC T+1 30% cut. Post-M&A integrations Horizon/Pacific shared ops $40-80 million synergies. Expense-to-AUM 24 bps record. Density improvements.

Operator: Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Goldman Sachs.

Raj Patel: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Emily Wong: Good question, Raj. Robust framework monitors MiFID II, PRIIPs, SFDR Level 3, SEC T+1/private gates, CSRC China. Enhanced vol/credit/ESG risks, dynamic hedging 15% vol cut, stress 20% drawdown. Vulnerabilities addressed via overlays, illiquidity premiums. Retention high post-reg shifts.

Operator: Our next question comes from Karen Wong with JPMorgan.

Karen Wong: How are you leveraging technology to improve investment performance?

David Patel: Key focus, Karen. AI Horizon Analytics ESG/quant signals tracking <1.5%, NLP 10k transcripts thematic 25% allocs AI/decarb outperforming 250 bps MSCI. ApexOne cloud OMS sub-ms execution, predictive flows, robo $65 billion 35% growth. Client360 CRM personalization NPS 72. Tokenized alts fractional. Cybersecurity posture strengthened, alpha/ML portfolio construction 15% cost red.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management Inc. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
